intro: German compounds are built right to left: the last element (Determinatum) is the head and gives gender and plural; everything before it (Determinans) specifies — der Arbeitsmarkt is a Markt, die Buchhandlung a Handlung. Between the parts sits a linking element (Fugenelement) whose choice is historical rather than grammatical: -s- after -ung / -heit / -keit / -schaft / -ion / -tät and many masculine/neuter nouns (Prüfungsordnung, Arbeitsmarkt, Liebesbrief, Geschwindigkeitsbegrenzung), -n- / -en- after most feminine nouns in -e and weak masculines (Sonnenbrille, Frauenarzt, Studentenwerk), -e- after some nouns with an -e plural (Hundehütte, Schweinebraten, Tageszeitung with -es-), -er- after nouns with an -er plural (Kindergarten, Bücherregal), and nothing at all in many (Buchhandlung, Haustür). Compounds are also made ad hoc — Bahnhofsbuchhandlungskette — and decoded by finding the head and peeling leftward. This quiz gives the parts (or the phrase) and asks for the compound with its correct joint. In formal writing you form them for concision (die Geschwindigkeitsbegrenzung instead of die Begrenzung der Geschwindigkeit) and read them at speed.
tips[0].title: Head last: gender, plural, meaning
tips[0].text: der Arbeitsmarkt (Markt: der) · die Buchhandlung (Handlung: die) · das Bücherregal (Regal: das). Plural of the head: Arbeitsmärkte. Meaning: a market for labour, a shop for books — read from the right.
tips[0].check.why: The last element decides: a Haustürschlüssel is a Schlüssel, and der Schlüssel is masculine, even though die Haustür comes first.
tips[1].title: Fugen-s: after -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -ion, -tät, and many others
tips[1].text: Prüfungsordnung, Freiheitsstatue, Möglichkeitsform, Wissenschaftsfreiheit, Informationsfluss, Universitätsstadt · also Arbeitsmarkt, Liebesbrief, Geburtstag, Verkehrsamt, Jahreszeit, Bundestag. No -s- after most feminine nouns not ending in those suffixes (Buchhandlung? no: Buch is neuter and takes none).
tips[1].trap: the Fugen-s is not a genitive, though it looks like one: Arbeitsmarkt (not 'the market of work' grammatically), Liebesbrief (Liebe is feminine and has no genitive -s). It's a joint, not a case.
tips[1].check.why: Nouns in -ung take the Fugen-s, even though Zeitung is feminine and has no genitive -s.
tips[2].title: -n-/-en-, -e-, -er-, or nothing
tips[2].text: -n-/-en-: Sonnenbrille, Frauenarzt, Straßenbahn, Studentenwerk, Menschenrecht · -e-: Hundehütte, Schweinebraten, Pferdestall, Tagebuch (and -es- in Tageszeitung) · -er-: Kindergarten, Bücherregal, Bilderbuch · nothing: Buchhandlung, Haustür, Handschuh, Bergsteiger.
tips[2].check.why: Kind has the plural Kinder, and it joins with -er-, as in Kindergarten.
tips[3].title: Decode leftward, then rebuild
tips[3].text: Bundesverfassungsgericht: Gericht ← Verfassung(s) ← Bund(es). A court, for the constitution, of the federation. Any monster compound falls apart from the right; and a phrase folds into one from the left: das Gericht für die Verfassung des Bundes → Bundesverfassungsgericht.
tips[3].check.why: Read from the right: Verlag is the head (a publisher), and Kinderbuch says what it publishes.
tips[3].visual.rows[0].en: a company (Gesellschaft) for … steamship travel on the Danube
remember[0]: Head last: gender and meaning from the right.
remember[1]: -s- after -ung/-heit/-keit/-schaft/-ion/-tät; -n- after feminines in -e; -er- after -er plurals; often nothing.

mistakes[2].why: No joint after Buch; gender from Handlung.
hook: Take any German monster word apart from the right, and build your own with the right joint between the pieces.
